primary_sources.observed_contract: _bootstrap_view replays only events.jsonl.1 and live events.jsonl; snapshot_mission_view performs bootstrap while holding the Mission View lock.
MISSION_BOOTSTRAP_MAX_BYTES is 8 MiB; _tail_jsonl reads only the final max_bytes and filters to projected canonical event types; _locked is the Mission View process/file lock.

rotation retains every generation as .2, .3, ... plus .1 and live; event_log_paths enumerates retained generations oldest-to-newest; _append holds events.lock through _maybe_roll, append, and Mission View projection.
update_mission_view_event acquires the Mission View lock before reducing and persisting a projected event.

material_findings.finding: Current cold bootstrap is not a full retained-history replay.
material_findings.basis: The pinned _bootstrap_view reads only events.jsonl.1 and events.jsonl, while the event logger intentionally retains older .2/.3/... generations. Each selected file is additionally truncated to the final 8 MiB by _tail_jsonl. Therefore projected events can remain durable in the canonical event log yet be absent from a cold Mission View bootstrap.
material_findings.scope: Source-level correctness gap in cold bootstrap/recovery only; no claim that normal online projection is dropping events and no production incident was observed.

material_findings.finding: Enumerating all generation path names and opening them later is not a stable rollover snapshot.
material_findings.basis: Rotation occurs under events.lock by renaming old .1 to the next free .N and live to .1. A reader that records [.2,.1,live] names without holding/pinning the event-log snapshot can have .1 and live rebound before open, omitting the former .1 even though it remains durable under a new .N name.
material_findings.scope: This is a defect in a naive proposed all-generation remediation, not an additional currently executed Mission View path: current code does not yet use event_log_paths for bootstrap. No production omission from this TOCTOU was observed.

material_findings.finding: Naively acquiring events.lock inside the existing Mission View bootstrap critical section would invert the writer lock order.
material_findings.basis: JsonlEventSink._append holds events.lock and then calls update_mission_view_event, which acquires the Mission View lock. snapshot_mission_view currently acquires the Mission View lock first. Adding events.lock acquisition inside that section would create mission->events versus writer events->mission ordering.
material_findings.scope: Lock-order risk of a proposed patch shape; no deadlock incident was observed. A safe implementation must preserve one global order or use a snapshot primitive that avoids inversion.

material_findings.finding: Opening/pinning retained files and capturing end offsets under events.lock is a plausible POSIX snapshot primitive, but not an implemented or validated Argus guarantee.
material_findings.basis: The repository explicitly targets POSIX flock in production paths, and rotation uses rename/replace under the event lock. The worker's pinned-descriptor idea is consistent with this structure, but no pinned Argus implementation or regression test was present in the inspected commit.
material_findings.scope: Do not promote this design direction to a completed fix or cross-platform guarantee.

downstream_implication.candidate_effect: clean-os-g1-006 is strengthened as a concrete recovery-observability defect with a sharper concurrency requirement. The proposed solution should be evaluated as two separable claims: lossless all-generation replay and a stable rollover snapshot with non-inverted locks.
downstream_implication.evidence_scope: pinned public source inspection only; no patch execution, production filesystem benchmark, or fault-injection reproduction was performed
